source.cite: K. Suzuki, R. Sudo, T. Feudel and W. Fichtner, IEEE Trans. Electron Devices 47(1), 44-49 (2000), doi 10.1109/16.817565
source.conditions: As into crystalline silicon, tilt 7 deg, rotation 22 deg, no cover oxide; parameters extracted by the authors from crystal-TRIM Monte Carlo tuned to SIMS (not from SIMS directly)

model: N(x) = (Phi - Phi_chan) n_a(x) + Phi_chan n_c(x) (eq. 9); n_a = joined half Gaussian (eq. 3, 5); n_c = JHG for x < Rpm + dRp2, kappa [JHG + h_m exp(-((x - Rpm)/L)^alpha)] beyond (eq. 4, 6, 7); each normalised on [0, inf) (eq. 8). Eq. 5 as printed lacks the squares: the joined half Gaussian of Gibbons and Mylroie (ref. 13) is h_m exp(-(x - Rpm)^2 / (2 dRp^2)).

fig4a.note: Fig. 4(a), page 46, digitised by the lead on 19 Nov 2026: page rendered at 600 dpi; frame from the pixels (0 nm and alpha 0.5 at row 1123, 200 nm and alpha 1.5 at row 165; 0 keV at column 368.5, 200 keV at 1416.5); markers found by filling outlines and morphological opening (15 px); at 40 keV the Rp and dRp2 markers merge (rows 1009-1049) and are split by marker size; at 200 keV the hollow markers sit on the frame and are read from their outlines. Below 40 keV the markers overlap too much to separate, so those energies are not used. Estimated reading uncertainty 1 nm (40 keV: 1.5 nm) and 0.01 in alpha.

fig4b_channel_dose.note: Fig. 4(b), page 46: log-log frame from the pixels (1e14 at row 17, 1e10 at row 932; dose 1e11 at column 400.5, 1e16 at 1539.0). All four curves read by eye from a crop with that calibration; checked against automatic marker centroids for 10 and 40 keV at doses where the markers are separate (agreement within 2 %). The 120 and 200 keV curves run close together. Reading uncertainty 5 %.
